# SPE round 5 plan: invoice extraction

Round 5 tests one fix. A new config S skips OCR cleanup on two-column layouts (P1, r04 F9). Q and R run again unchanged as controls. Config P is dropped (P3). The 15 handwriting invoices (P2) wait until the AP lead supplies reference fields for them.

I assumed round 4 ran 3 trials per cell. If it ran a different number, round 5 uses round 4's number.

## What round 4 showed

- Q hit. I predicted 0.91 and it measured 0.93.
- R missed. I predicted 0.95 and it measured 0.88. The naive guess of 0.90 was closer than my prediction.
- The Why that broke was "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals." Round 4 never measured scanned totals as a separate metric. It did show that the tool drops line items on two-column layouts (F9).
- The stop streak is 0 after the r04 miss. If every cell hits this round, the streak becomes 1.

## Specify

### Proposals

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1: skip OCR cleanup on two-column layouts | Adopt as config S | It targets F9. S differs from R in one thing only. |
| P2: add 15 scanned handwriting invoices | Defer (default) | The repo has no reference fields for these invoices, and only the AP lead can supply them. New tasks would also break the comparison with r04. Q's 0.93 is still 0.07 below the maximum, so the metric is not at a ceiling yet. The question is logged for the user. |
| P3: drop config P | Adopt | P trails Q on every metric in r04. S takes P's trial slots, so the total trial count stays the same. |

### Requirement table for spec.md, round 5

New IDs continue from the last ID in spec.md. This plan calls them N1 to N7. They get their real numbers when the table is written to spec.md.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | S is identical to R except for one change. S skips OCR cleanup on any invoice the layout detector marks as two-column. | r04 F9, P1 | Harness config diff check: S and R differ only in the `ocr_skip_two_column` flag |
| N2 | The layout detector flags every invoice that is tagged two-column | r04 F9 | Gate G3: detector output compared with the `layout` tag on all 60 invoices |
| N3 | On two-column invoices, S recovers line items as well as Q does | r04 F9 | `line_item_recall_2col` |
| N4 | S's field accuracy lands inside Q's band | r04 prediction log (Q measured 0.93) | `field_accuracy` |
| N5 | Scanned totals are measured as a separate metric. This tests the Why that broke in r04. | r04 "Which Why broke" | `scanned_total_acc` |
| N6 | Config P is retired. Q becomes the reference config. | P3 | The Workflow configs list contains only Q, R, and S |
| N7 | The task set is the same 60 invoices with the same AP lead reference fields as r04 | Default, so results compare with r04 | The task manifest hash matches r04 |

Before anyone writes the detector code, each invoice gets a `layout` tag (single-column or two-column) and a `scanned` tag. I tag them from the page images.

### Defaults and open decisions

| ID | Question | Default | Reason | Decides |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-r05-1 | Should round 5 add the 15 handwriting invoices (P2)? | Deferred | No reference fields exist for them yet. New tasks would break the comparison with r04. | The user, with the AP lead |
| D-r05-2 | Who tags layout and scanned? | Claude tags them from page images before the detector is written | The subset graders need the tags. The AP lead's reference fields do not record layout. | The user can override |
| D-r05-3 | How many trials per cell? | 3, the same as r04 | Everything stays fixed except the config change | Claude (default) |

The defaults go in the round 5 defaults table in spec.md. D-r05-1 goes in disagreements.md as an open decision.

## Predict

The configs are Q (the reference, unchanged), R (an unchanged control), and S (R plus the skip on two-column layouts). P is dropped. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

| Metric | Grader check | Q | R | S | Same as last round | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy | `field_accuracy`: a code check for normalized exact match on vendor, invoice number, date, line items, and total against the AP lead fields | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | Q 0.93, R 0.88, S 0.88 (R's value, because S is built on R) | Q and R did not change. S removes the F9 loss. I add nothing for a scanned-totals gain because r04 did not show one. |
| Line-item recall, two-column subset | `line_item_recall_2col`: a code check matching description, quantity, and amount | 0.95 ± 0.05 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | 0.95 ± 0.05 | The r04 values, computed in gate G2 | Q never runs cleanup. R still runs it on this subset and drops items (F9). S skips cleanup here, so it should match Q. R's band is wide because r04 did not report how many invoices are in the subset. |
| Total accuracy, scanned single-column subset | `scanned_total_acc`: a code check that the total matches to the cent | 0.90 ± 0.05 | 0.90 ± 0.05 | 0.90 ± 0.05 | The r04 values, computed in gate G2 | This metric tests R's broken Why directly. I predict no gain from cleanup until a round measures one. R and S both run cleanup on this subset, so they should match each other. |

Gate G2 regrades r04 outputs to get the naive values for the two subset metrics. G2 runs before any r05 trial starts. These values go into prediction-log.md. They do not go into the saved prediction file.

## Evaluate

### Steps after approval, in order

1. **Specify.** Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md` with "go again" and the pasted text, word for word. Add the round 5 requirement table and the defaults table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Add D-r05-1 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Make a local commit: `spe r05: specify`.
2. **Predict.** Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`, starting from `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` and leaving the draft file as it is. The yaml's first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds round 5, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs Q, R, and S, every number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. Make a local commit: `spe r05: predict`.
3. **Build S and the harness.** Add the `ocr_skip_two_column` flag and the layout detector. Add the `layout` and `scanned` tags to the task metadata. Write `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 5`. No prompt text contains a hand-written round number.
4. **Gates.** Run them in this order. If any gate fails, I stop and report to you.
   - G1, grader selftest. The oracle output passes all three checks. Empty and wrong outputs fail all three.
   - G2, control. Regrade the r04 outputs with the r05 graders. Field accuracy must come out at Q 0.93 and R 0.88, within 0.01. Record the r04 subset values as the naive guesses.
   - G3, detector. Run the detector on all 60 invoices. It must flag every invoice tagged two-column. False positives are allowed, but each one gets listed.
   - G4, dry run on 3 cells: S on one two-column invoice, R on one scanned invoice, and Q on one single-column invoice. Check the output schema, the grader run, and the transcript scan.
5. Make a local commit of the S code, tags, harness, and gate logs: `spe r05: evaluate`. Then launch the Workflow.

### Workflow arguments

- `ROUND`: 5
- Configs: Q, R, and S, all pinned to the same Sonnet 5.5 model ID as r04
- Tasks: the 60 invoices, with the manifest unchanged from r04
- Trials: 3 per cell. A cell counts as split when its trials disagree on any field. Split cells get up to 2 extra trials.
- Trial output schema: vendor, invoice_number, date, line_items[], total, and po_mismatch flags
- Graders: the three code checks above. This round needs no judge because code can check every metric.
- Isolation: trials cannot read the reference fields, grader code, tags, or predictions. A transcript scan voids any trial that touched them.
- Budget cap: 1.25 times the actual r04 spend. The Workflow skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs the skip.
- End steps: failure analysis on every miss, then a completeness critic

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The round runs 3 configs × 60 invoices × 3 trials = 540 trials, plus up to 2 extra trials on each split cell. That is the same count as r04 because S takes P's place. I expect the spend to be close to r04's. S skips the cleanup call on two-column invoices, so S should cost a little less than R.

## Learn, after the completion notice

- Add the round 5 section to `spe/prediction-log.md` with Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer for every cell. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. The section says plainly whether the naive guess beat my predictions again.
- Update F9's Fix line in `spe/failures.md` with the S result. New failure types start at F10. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure, and its original and regraded numbers sit side by side.
- Add a "Proposed for round 6" table to spec.md and write `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. D-r05-1 (P2) goes back to you there if it is still open.
- Update `spe/README.md`. Make a local commit, `spe r05: learn`, and tag it `spe-r05`.
- Ceiling check: if every config scores 1.00 on a metric, I record those predictions as not scorable and check once for a leak or a grader bug. Then I tell you the tasks no longer separate the configs.

## Halt conditions

I halt and report on any of these: the budget cap, a leaked answer key, a failed gate, a broken grader, or a decision only you can make. All commits stay local, and I do not push.
